pa_sb1346.title: Pennsylvania SB 1346: ADUs on single-family detached lots outside Philadelphia and Pittsburgh

label.text: Eligible lots

meaning.text: Lots the rule reaches: existing homes of the building types in scope, counted as lots.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of eligible lots = sum over building types in scope of [census homes of that type / homes per building] x lot-count correction x (1 - already-legal share) x share of the tract inside the scenario's places = 2,291,662 lots, 2,400,451 lots, 2,516,496 lots

label.text: Lots with room for an ADU

meaning.text: Of those, lots with enough yard for a backyard home of the required size.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots with room = sum over building types of eligible lots x fit share f(type, area type) = 1,482,152 lots, 1,739,882 lots, 1,951,173 lots

label.text: Lots where an ADU is feasible

meaning.text: Of those, lots where rent would pay for building one, or where the owner would build one for family anyway.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of feasible lots = lots with room x p, where p = p_rent + family-use share x (1 - p_rent) and p_rent = share of the tract's cash rents at or above break-even rent / (one-bedroom ratio x new-unit premium) = 105,438 lots, 188,960 lots, 302,978 lots

label.text: ADUs built 2027-2031

meaning.text: Of those, the ones expected to be built over the five years, with a slow start while owners learn about the new right.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of ADUs built = feasible lots x yearly take-up h x sum over 2027-2031 of ramp(t) x ADUs per lot n = 3,733 units, 8,505 units, 16,573 units

label.text: Net added units 2027-2031

meaning.text: What is left after taking out homes that would have been built anyway: the reform's own addition.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of net added units = ADUs built x (1 - displacement share x) = 3,276 units, 7,530 units, 14,589 units

general.title: What these estimates cannot tell you

items.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
The baseline repeats recent permit trends under today's rules. It does not predict a recession or a boom.
Counties without a permit office, or with imputed permit counts, carry the Census Bureau's estimates.
Whether an ADU fits on a given lot: the fit test is a share for each census tract, not a site plan.
Septic limits, steep slopes, flood zones, historic districts and private deed rules, none of which are in the fit test.
Whether towns slow approvals or add new hurdles.
How quickly owners take up the new right. This is the widest assumption and is not yet checked against places like this state.
The bill is not law. The estimate assumes it passes as written and applies from the start of the period.
Philadelphia and Pittsburgh are outside the Municipalities Planning Code, so the bill leaves their rules as they are.

title.text: How many more homes would Pennsylvania permit?

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms
Baseline: homes permitted under today's rules
With the reforms

body.text: Over 2027–2031, Pennsylvania would likely permit between 3,300 and 15,000 more homes (2.4–14%) with Pennsylvania SB 1346 passed, on top of a baseline of 67,000–180,000 homes expected under today's rules.

title.text: Pennsylvania SB 1346: ADUs on single-family detached lots outside Philadelphia and Pittsburgh: Adds a lot

cites.value: Pennsylvania SB 1346: ADUs on single-family detached lots outside Philadelphia and Pittsburgh
cites.shown: Pennsylvania SB 1346: ADUs on single-family detached lots outside Philadelphia and Pittsburgh

label.text: More homes permitted, this reform alone
Eligible lots

meaning.text: Lots the rule reaches: existing homes of the building types in scope, counted as lots.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of eligible lots = sum over building types in scope of [census homes of that type / homes per building] x lot-count correction x (1 - already-legal share) x share of the tract inside the scenario's places = 2,291,662 lots, 2,400,451 lots, 2,516,496 lots

label.text: Lots with room for an ADU

meaning.text: Of those, lots with enough yard for a backyard home of the required size.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots with room = sum over building types of eligible lots x fit share f(type, area type) = 1,482,152 lots, 1,739,882 lots, 1,951,173 lots

label.text: Lots where an ADU is feasible

meaning.text: Of those, lots where rent would pay for building one, or where the owner would build one for family anyway.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of feasible lots = lots with room x p, where p = p_rent + family-use share x (1 - p_rent) and p_rent = share of the tract's cash rents at or above break-even rent / (one-bedroom ratio x new-unit premium) = 105,438 lots, 188,960 lots, 302,978 lots

label.text: ADUs built 2027-2031

meaning.text: Of those, the ones expected to be built over the five years, with a slow start while owners learn about the new right.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of ADUs built = feasible lots x yearly take-up h x sum over 2027-2031 of ramp(t) x ADUs per lot n = 3,733 units, 8,505 units, 16,573 units

label.text: Net added units 2027-2031

meaning.text: What is left after taking out homes that would have been built anyway: the reform's own addition.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of net added units = ADUs built x (1 - displacement share x) = 3,276 units, 7,530 units, 14,589 units

body.text: Middle estimate: 5.8% more homes than the baseline. “Adds a lot” means at least 5%.
Lots the rule reaches: existing homes of the building types in scope, counted as lots.

title.text: What these estimates cannot tell you

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms

body.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
Decision support, not a forecast. Not an official state document.
